summary.en: The Ottoman Empire recognised an independent Greek kingdom and accepted a frontier running from the Gulf of Arta to the Pagasetic Gulf. This was a more generous line than the London Protocol of 1830 had drawn. The new state held the Peloponnese, Attica, Central Greece, Euboea and the Cyclades, and roughly a third of the Greek speaking population of the region lived inside it.

body_html.en:
The London Protocol of February 1830 had made Greece independent but drawn its frontier along the Aspropotamos and Spercheios rivers, leaving Acarnania and much of Central Greece outside. The Powers' choice of Otto of Bavaria as king in May 1832 came with a commitment to a better line.

At Constantinople in July the Ottoman plenipotentiaries accepted the Arta to Volos frontier in exchange for an indemnity of forty million piastres, paid from the loan the Powers had guaranteed to the new kingdom. The line stood, with only the Ionian addition, until 1881.
